title: 1965 AHSME Problem 31
statement: The number of real values of \(x\) satisfying the equality \((\log_a x)(\log_b x)=\log_a b,\) where \(a\) and \(b\) are positive constants different from \(1,\) is:

solutions.text:
Change of base gives \[ \frac{\ln x}{\ln a}\frac{\ln x}{\ln b} =\frac{\ln b}{\ln a}. \] Since the denominators are nonzero, \((\ln x)^2=(\ln b)^2.\) Thus \(x=b\) or \(x=\frac{1}{b}.\) These are distinct because \(b\ne1,\) so there are two values.

Therefore, the correct answer is C.
